LESSON: USE OF LETTERS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.8: Use of letters
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Use of letters, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we represent information using letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Represent various items from diverse geographical locations using letters. Those with poor motor coordination or missing limbs could use adapted writing materials or adapted digital devices to perform the task. They could also use assistive technology to carry out the

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Represent various items from diverse geographical locations using letters. Those with poor motor coordination or missing limbs could use adapted writing materials or adapted digital devices to perform the task. They could also use assistive technology to carry out the

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Use of letters together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: learner represents various items from diverse geographical locations using letters.

• Communication and collaboration: learner forms expressions to represent real life situation.

Values:
Respect: learner gives each other a chance to play digital games involving expressions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner works harmoniously in a group to represent various items from diverse geographical locations using

letters to enhance social cohesion.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate the concept of letters to the skills of reading and writing in languages.
